earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog med: only Z'graggen 1975/1980 survey wordlists; no descriptive material.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (sealang.net/archives/pl/pdf/)
sources.note: Survey-wide disclaimer only, sec. 1.3.3 p. 7: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Bagupi is not yet distinguished as a language in this 1971 volume (Hanseman list lacks it); no per-language stress statement.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. 1 v. hdl 1885/130077 (Open Access; PDF 4.6 MB + scanned text bundle).
sources.note: Only the survey-wide transcription note (text-bundle line 214, thesis p. 13): stress was not marked because its patterning had not been established - identical in substance to PL C-19 sec. 1.3.3 p. 7 already held by the project. No per-language prosodic statement, and nothing on Bagupi.

sources.citation: Greenhill, S. J. (ed.). TransNewGuinea.org, language page 'Bagupi' (transnewguinea.org/language/bagupi)
sources.note: Sources: Z'graggen (1980) only; re-keyed lexicon without stress marks.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG. Languages of Papua New Guinea: 'Language: Bagupi' [bpi] resource page (pnglanguages.sil.org/resources/languages/language/bpi), read 2026-09-20 via text proxy.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content: province, ISO code, Ethnologue link, and two links ('Bagupi in the SIL-PNG Archives', 'Bagupi Publications Available Online') that lead to an automated-access block CAPTCHA. Google's index of pnglanguages.sil.org shows no /resources/archives/ item naming Bagupi, and OLAC (2025 capture held by the project) lists no SIL item for bpi, so no SIL OPD/survey/data paper is known to exist.

sources.citation: OLAC: Resources in and about the Bagupi language [bpi] (language-archives.org/language/bpi, Internet Archive copy, up-to-date May 2025)
sources.note: Inventory only: Rosetta Project Swadesh list, transnewguinea.org, Glottolog, Ethnologue; no SIL archive item, no description.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Appears only in the annotated classification list (speaker figure + best available source, here a wordlist), confirming no phonology exists; the prosody overview (sec. 2.4, 'In languages of the Madang and Finisterre-Huon groups.. tone and pitch accent are largely absent') is group-level and names no target language.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, ANU. xiii+476 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-D90.
sources.note: No phonology content. The language index gives for Bagupi only 'W&H 1981, Z'graggen 1975' (Wurm & Hattori atlas; Z'graggen 1975); the Z'graggen author entry adds a 1971 mimeo 'New Guinea comparative word list' (Anthropos-Institut, 48 pp., the elicitation schedule) and '1972-74 Comparative wordlists of the Madang District.. see the PL version'. Confirms independently that no descriptive source on Bagupi existed as of 1996.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-D32 (sealang.net/archives/pl/pdf/)
sources.note: Nothing. Intro sec. 6 (p. viii): 'The transcription is semi-phonemic'; lists fluctuating sounds per language incl. Bagupi (p. ix); no mention of stress/accent/tone; Bagupi (C21) forms carry vowel length but no stress marks (visual check of p. 2).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38. DOI 10.15144/PL-C38.569
sources.note: Nothing; classification only (sec. 2.8.2.2.1.2.4, p. 582 lists Bagupi among 19 Hanseman languages; population C21 Bagupi 51; pronoun and 8-item comparative rows).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975b. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-B41
sources.note: Nothing; village/language gazetteer (C21 Bagupi 58: Bagupi 25, Opi 33).

Metadata; refs are Z'graggen 1969/1975/1980, Pawley & Hammarstrom 2017, Pick 2020 (subclassification), Campbell et al. 2022 (AES); no descriptive reference (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).
